title.narrative: COVID-19: Active Response and Expenditure Support Program

description.narrative: The CARES Program will provide budget support to the government for implementing its countercyclical expenditure program for mitigating the adverse social and economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The government?s COVID-19 countercyclical expenditure program of $351 million consists of (i) COVID-19 pandemic response plan targeting the upgrading and provision of health facilities and supplies to support public health ($97 million); (ii) a COVID-19 social protection package for the vulnerable population such as the unemployed, poor and vulnerable households, gender-based violence survivors, and expatriate migrant workers, and subsidies to households on electricity and water bills ($124 million); and (iii) a COVID-19 economic response, providing subsidized working capital to the self-employed and businesses ($130 million).

description.narrative: Adverse socioeconomic effect of COVID-19 for poor and vulnerable groups mitigated

By August 2020, 10,000 poor and vulnerable people (of whom at least 25% are women) benefited from at least one economic assistance program under the government's COVID-19 response plan Data Source: MOF report Actual value:
By December 2020, at least 70% of businesses and 75% of women-led businesses that received working capital support still in business Data Source: MOF report Baseline value: no support provided

By December 2020, at least 80% of surveyed beneficiaries supported by one or more support package are “generally satisfied” (using 5-point scale survey supported by online and/or IVR system), with data disaggregated by sex, income group, industry, and rural and/or urban Data Source: MOF report and beneficiary satisfaction survey Baseline value: not applicable
By October 2020, COVID-19 confirmed cases doubling rate improved to 30 days or more Data Source: MOF report Baseline value: 4 days
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Economic assistance measures implemented Indicator: By August 2020, 100% of eligible applications for working capital support from MSMEs and self-employed applicants with an annual turnover below Rf10,000,000 in 2019 (of which at least 18% are women-led businesses) under COVID-19 Viyafaari Ehee Loan scheme received the loan within 3 weeks from submission of completed applications (within 2 weeks from submission of completed applications for female applicants) Progress/Status: Total eligible applicants (from April 2020 to December 2020): 2,203 Applicants that are women-led businesses: 577 (26%) Applications processed within 3 weeks: 1,352 (61%) Applications of women-led businesses processed within 2 weeks: 192 (33%)
Data Source: MOF, MED compliance reports Actual value:

Output: Economic assistance measures implemented Indicator: By August 2020, at least 90% of eligible applications for working capital support from businesses and tourist resorts with annual turnover in 2019 above Rf10,000,000 (of which at least 10% are from female applicants) under COVID-19 Recovery Scheme received the loan within 3 weeks from submission of completed applications Progress/Status: Eligible applicants for the working capital support (from April 2021 to December 2020): 441 Eligible applicants processed within 3 weeks: 230 (52%) Applications that are women-led: 32 (7%) Data Source: MOF, MED compliance reports Actual value:

Output: Social protection measures implemented Indicator: By December 2020, all COVID-19 patients (national and expatriates) provided with health coverage under health financing scheme (Aasandha) including outpatient and inpatient care Progress/Status: From April to December 2020, around 1,275 patients have been covered by Aasandha. Expatriate COVID-19 patients received assistance through other Government health financing schemes, as Aasandha covers nationals only. Data Source: MOF, MGFSS compliance reports Actual value:

Output: Social protection measures implemented Indicator: By June 2020, 100% of eligible applicants are paid full allowance within 3 weeks from submission of completed applications (within 2 weeks from submission of completed applications for vulnerable women and differently abled applicants), in line with the COVID-19 Income Support Allowance Program Progress/Status: Total eligible applicants from April to December 2020 - 84,584 [men 54,678 (65%) and women 29,906 (35%)]. Eligible applicants from April to December processed within 3 weeks - 18,745 (22%)
Application from women from April to December 2020 processed within 2 weeks - 1,929 (9%) Data Source: MOF, MGFSS compliance reports Actual value:

Output: Social protection measures implemented Indicator: By May 2020, at least 45,000 households provided with 40% electricity subsidy and 30% water subsidy for April 2020-May 2020 Progress/Status: Electricity subsidy: In April 2020, 92,773 households received electric subsidy, 93,383 in May and 90,047 in June. Water subsidy: In April 2020, 30,157 households received water subsidy, 52,613 in May and 28,131 in June.
Data Source: MOF, MGFSS compliance reports Actual value:

Output: Social protection measures implemented Indicator: By August 2020, at least 5 accommodation blocks for survivors of GBV within the family and child service centers in Malé and outer atolls ehabilitated and operational (with capacity of 100 individuals) Progress/Status: 3 accommodation blocks for survivors of GBV have initiated services as of 12 May 2021. Data Source: MOF, MGFSS compliance reports Actual value:

Output: COVID-19 health response measures implemented Indicator: By August 2020, at least 400 isolation beds in health facilities made available with separate wards for men and women Progress/Status: 853 isolation beds (831 beds and 22 rooms) made available as of May 17, 2021. Private rooms allowed for gender segregation. Data Source: MOF, MOH compliance reports Actual value:

Output: COVID-19 health response measures implemented Indicator: By August 2020, COVID-19 testing facilities set up in 5 regional hospitals across 5 zones Progress/Status: Testing facilities set up in 19 regional hospitals across 11 zones as of 23, February 2021. - 8 facilities in the central zone -11 facilities in different atolls Data Source: MOF, MOH compliance reports Actual value:

Output: COVID-19 health response measures implemented Indicator: By August 2020, 200 critical care beds made available for COVID-19 treatment Progress/Status: 113 critical beds available as of May 17, 2021. This consisted of 20 beds in the Greater Male region and 93 beds in the Atolls. Data Source: MOF, MOH compliance reports Actual value:

Output: COVID-19 health response measures implemented Indicator: By August 2020, testing capacity increased to 800/day Progress/Status: Testing capacity was increased to 8,840 tests per day from 7,500 as of 23 February2021. Data Source: MOF, MOH compliance reports Actual value:

Output: Social protection measures implemented Indicator: By December 2020, at least 15,000 migrant workers transferred to safer accommodations in greater Malé, with separate accommodation for women Progress/Status: 9,391 migrant workers were given temporary accommodation as of 23 February 2021. Data Source: MOF, MGFSS compliance reports Actual value:

Output: COVID-19 response governance mechanisms strengthened Indicator: By 31 March 2021, the annual report of the COVID-19 response trust fund published, including information on monthly progress in COVID-19 response for the first 3 months, and quarterly progress thereafter with data disaggregated by sex, age, and disability Progress/Status: MOF has regularly reported on the weekly performance of COVID-19 related expenditure. A first draft of the annual report has been prepared by MOF and is currently in the finalization stage. Data Source: MOF compliance report Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: COVID-19 response governance mechanisms strengthened Indicator: By December 2020, a report identifying M&E capacity gaps for relevant government programs and strengthening of M&E systems containing recommendations for strengthening of M&E systems with data disaggregated by sex, age and disability completed and endorsed by government Progress/Status: The M&E capacity gaps report is drafted with support from ADB M&E and Gender Consultants. Discussions with implementing agencies are underway to finalize the report. Data Source: MOF compliance report Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Social protection measures implemented Indicator: By August 2020, cash assistance provided for 3 months to 4,000 poor and vulnerable households, including at least 1,500 vulnerable households led by single, widowed, divorced, or differently abled women Progress/Status: From May 2020 to January 2021, cash assistance was provided to 143,578 households (single parent: 33,949; foster parent: 1,344; food assistance: 1,507; disability allowance: 106,778)
For April 2021, 7,018 households were led by single, widowed, divorced, or differently-abled women.
Data Source: MOF, MGFSS compliance reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2020 Target value: 4000
